To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed method can successfully separate drug addicted subjects from controls by using temporal information in fMRI data; (ii) the proposed method is robust to the number of training subjects; (iii) the proposed method provides a valid tool for clinical classification of psychopatologies; (iv) the proposed method has a general application in fMRI data analysis and can be extended to other applications.

the proposed method is able to: 1. extract discriminative features for group classification, 2. exploit temporal information for improved performance, 3. provide statistical validation of the classification performance and 4. provide neuroscientific validation of classification performance by demonstrating that the method generalizes well to new subjects.
the proposed method can be successfully applied to fMRI data to identify drug addiction, and that it can be generalized to other applications.
